nodes.label: Mathematics II — Textbook for Grade XI (Egyptian Baccalaureate, 2nd Year), Part One, English
Coefficients in binomial expansions
nodes.description: Calculate combinations nCr and determine the term or the coefficient of a specified term in the expansion of (a+b)^n.

nodes.label: Expand using Binomial Theorem
nodes.description: Expand expressions of the form (a+b)^n in full using the Binomial Theorem.

nodes.label: Multinomial Theorem coefficients
nodes.description: Determine the coefficient of a specified term in the expansion of a three-term expression such as (a+b+c)^n using the Multinomial Theorem.

nodes.label: Prove identities with the binomial expansion
nodes.description: Prove identities involving binomial coefficients (sums of combinations) and divisibility by expanding (1+x)^n and substituting an appropriate value for x.

nodes.label: Polynomial long division
nodes.description: Divide one polynomial by another using the long division algorithm, state the quotient and the remainder, and treat other variables as constants when dividing as a polynomial in x.

nodes.label: Use A = BQ + R
nodes.description: Use A = B × Q + R to find the dividend A or the divisor B when the quotient and the remainder are given.

nodes.label: Reduce rational expressions
nodes.description: Simplify a rational expression by factorising the numerator and denominator and reducing common factors.

nodes.label: Multiply and divide rational expressions
nodes.description: Calculate the product or quotient of rational expressions by factorising, using the reciprocal of the divisor, and cancelling common factors.

nodes.label: Add and subtract rational expressions
nodes.description: Add and subtract rational expressions with different denominators by factorising the denominators, finding a common denominator, and reducing the result.

nodes.label: Simplify compound fractions
nodes.description: Simplify compound fractions by multiplying the numerator and denominator by the same expression to give a single rational expression.

nodes.label: Find constants in identities
nodes.description: Find the values of constants in an identity in x by arranging both sides in descending powers of x (clearing denominators where needed) and comparing coefficients of terms of the same degree.

nodes.label: Prove equalities by simplifying
nodes.description: Prove an algebraic equality by simplifying the LHS and RHS respectively until they become the same expression.

nodes.label: Prove conditional equalities
nodes.description: Prove an equality that holds under a given condition by expressing one variable in terms of the others from the condition and substituting to eliminate it.

nodes.label: Prove with proportions
nodes.description: Prove equalities and find values of expressions given a proportion, by letting the ratios equal a constant k and substituting.

nodes.label: Prove conditional inequalities
nodes.description: Prove a conditional inequality by calculating LHS − RHS, factorising it and using the given conditions (e.g. a > b rewritten as a − b > 0) to show the result is positive.

nodes.label: Prove by completing the square
nodes.description: Prove an inequality for all real numbers by completing the square to form X² or X² + Y², and determine when equality holds.

nodes.label: Prove inequalities with roots
nodes.description: Prove inequalities containing square roots by calculating (LHS)² − (RHS)², showing LHS > 0 and RHS > 0, and determine when equality holds.

nodes.label: Apply the AM-GM inequality
nodes.description: Apply the AM-GM inequality for positive a and b to prove inequalities, determine when equality holds (a = b), and find maximum values such as an area.

questions.stem: Consider the first rows of Pascal's triangle, and notice how the number of terms changes in each horizontal row as shown in the figure. If you follow this pattern, how many terms will there be in the tenth row?
solution: The figure labels each row with its number of terms: Row 0 has 1 term, Row 1 has 2 terms, Row 2 has 3 terms.
So Row n has n + 1 terms.
The figure labels Row 10 as having 11 terms.

questions.stem: Challenge — Find the Height: A cuboid shaped box of volume $4x^3+4x^2-9x-9$. If the area of its base is $2x^2-x-3$, write its height in terms of $x$.

questions.stem: Find the polynomials $A$ and $B$ that satisfy the following conditions. When $A$ is divided by $x^2 - 2x - 1$, the quotient is $x+3$ and remainder is $-2x+5$
solution: A is divided by B = x^2 - 2x - 1, so Q = x + 3 and R = -2x + 5.
Multiply every term of the first bracket by every term of the second: x^3 + 3x^2 - 2x^2 - 6x - x - 3.

questions.stem: Find the polynomials $A$ and $B$ that satisfy the following conditions. When $4x^3 + 8x - 9$ is divided by $B$, the quotient is $2x-3$ and remainder is $x+15$
solution: Here A = 4x^3 + 8x - 9, Q = 2x - 3 and R = x + 15.
Subtract the remainder from A: B(2x - 3) = 4x^3 + 8x - 9 - x - 15 = 4x^3 + 7x - 24.

questions.stem: Find the values of the constants $a$, $b$, and $c$ such that the following equations are identities in $x$. $\frac{3x+1}{(x+2)(x-3)}=\frac{a}{x+2}+\frac{b}{x-3}$

solution: $x^2+6=ax^2+(2a+b)x+(a+b+c)$ (side note: Rearrange the RHS in descending powers of $x$.)
Therefore, $1=a$, $0=2a+b$, $6=a+b+c$ (side note: Compare the coefficients of terms with the same degree.)
Solving this system of equations gives $a=1$, $b=-2$, and $c=7$ (side notes: If there is no $x$ term, consider the coefficient to be 0; Solve the simultaneous equations for $a$, $b$, and $c$.)

$3x+1=a(x-3)+b(x+2)$ (side note: Rearrange the RHS in descending powers of $x$.)
Solving this system of equations gives $a=1$ and $b=2$
